label: Personal origins in Aquinas and the Greek creed
summary: Read the materialized Greek creed (DS 150, arts. 2 and 8) and compared its two professions with Aquinas's account in ST I qq27–30, q32 a1 and q37 a1. A relation to oneself as known or loved differs from the origin of a subsisting Word or Love. Aquinas explains the personal count once immanent origins, subsistence and relative opposition are granted. He locates the analogy's force in its fit with revealed doctrine. The creed's Spirit clause specifies procession from the Father and joint worship with Father and Son. It leaves Aquinas's common-spiration argument to further theology. Precise locators and interpretive limits are in docs/notes/de-ente-esse-source-1628.md, section ‘From one divine nature to personal distinctions’. The evidence IDs identify the existing creed readings. No proof or new source binding follows from this comparison.
